proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a signed-family spectral frontier, invariant-calibration selector, noncommuting benchmark and noise-operator obstruction; verified scalar IFT/algebraic support repairs introduced no causal assumptions. Final D0.5 triaged incremental ceiling 6.4 below the fixed field floor and left two central Fan instantiations unresolved, making the physical-edge and all downstream frontier/attainment claims conditional. Independent main validity confirmed downgraded STOP: no Lean/F stages, no kernel refutation, no bounded tier-lifting route; retry requires a substantive new contribution axis and a faithful proof repair.
tldr: Noise-corrected experiment summaries can be unbiased for causal effect covariance while their leading direction remains unrecovered. The results compute the globally optimized recovery threshold of matched signed scatters with finite calibration and two possibly noncommuting noise components whose common basis is unknown. The physical matrix-resolvent system and original-record secular equation give the overlap limit, with zero overlap at critical equality. The complete minimizing set and noncommuting benchmark are certified, and quotient-based calibration yields one attainable procedure above the optimized threshold. A both-group operator-estimation obstruction distinguishes original calibration from supplied full-noise subtraction. This frontier applies to the declared raw-scatter family.
gap: Fixed signed covariance maps and positive isotropic PCA optimization do not by themselves determine the global physical threshold, its optimizer geometry and attainable tuning in this hidden joint-noise model.
fill: The integrated kernel computes a physical signed recovery frontier, certifies every threshold minimizer and a noncommuting benchmark, and attains the oracle regime from five calibration-estimable conjugacy invariants. The supporting obstruction concerns full noise estimation, rather than all-method effect recovery.
